Prove instead the theorem over the explicit noiseless local experiment used below. Establish population and empirical basin entry as conclusions by: (a) proving a global uniform-law distortion gap of order K^-3 times squared ordered-codebook distance, or at least an off-basin gap c K^-5 outside radius c'/K; (b) transferring that gap to the near-uniform tilted densities; (c) applying a global Bernstein/entropy peeling argument before invoking local quadratic growth; (d) deriving deltaC and the QC Voronoi-switching score discrepancy after localization. Do not add basin entry, a separation factor, or the claimed rate as an assumption.

4. For thm:fano-membership, use the already approved negative standardized-score likelihood tilt with nu_n=0. At nu_n=0 the tilt is a bounded U-only density tilt, so b(u)=u, overlap, conditional outcome laws, and common oracle nuisances are unchanged exactly. Prove normalization, bounded-feature membership, unique optimizer, local curvature, margin, relative variance/covariance stability, KL control, and pairwise gain separation. Correct the first-order sign to minus. Prove any growth restriction from the explicit uniform-risk and Hessian calculations; do not insert delta_n K_n^a -> 0 as an assumed crux.

5. For thm:matched-width-frontier, retain the covariance-aware multiplier upper bound and the rectangular-band Fano lower bound jointly over the explicit nu_n=0 tilted experiment. State the final sufficient regime through the corrected Xi_n; an acceptable explicit corollary is K_n^5 log(K_n) sqrt(log(nK_n))/sqrt(n) -> 0 and log^7(nK_n)/n -> 0. The exact covariance and width calculations may remain uniform over nu_n in [0,1/4], but do not claim a matched within-class lower bound for positive/noise-dominated nu_n unless a separate bounded-feature-safe conditional-outcome construction is proved.

Pollard 1982 Quantization and the Method of k-Means pp. 199–204 proves fixed-k global-ERM consistency using uniqueness, compactness, and a uniform strong law, not a row-uniform basin gap. Liu–Pagès 2020 Theorems 4–5 pp. 8–10 and Proposition 11/Theorem 12 pp. 12–14 provide a fixed-level optimizer-localization template requiring optimizer convergence and local positive Hessians, not uniform K<=K_n localization.

Fix an integer \(V\geq3\), independent of \(n\), and a deterministic partition \(\{\mathcal I_v:1\leq v\leq V\}\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).  For each \(v\), fix disjoint nuisance-training and codebook-fitting sets \(\mathcal T_v,\mathcal Q_v\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal I_v\), each having cardinality at least a fixed positive multiple of \(n\).  Fit \(\widehat e_v,\widehat\mu_{0,v},\widehat\mu_{1,v}\) using only \(\mathcal T_v\), put
\[
 \widehat e_v^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=\min\{1-\epsilon/2,\max(\epsilon/2,\widehat e_v(x))\},
 \qquad
 \widehat b_v(x)=\min\!\left[1,\max\!\left\{0,
 \frac{\widehat\mu_{1,v}(x)-\widehat\mu_{0,v}(x)+1}{2}\right\}\right],
\]
and define, for \(o=(x,a,y)\),
\[
 \widehat\zeta_v(o)=\frac12\left[
 \frac{a\{y-\widehat\mu_{1,v}(x)\}}{\widehat e_v^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)}
 -\frac{(1-a)\{y-\widehat\mu_{0,v}(x)\}}{1-\widehat e_v^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)}\right].
\]
For \(C\in\mathcal C_K\), let \(q_C(u)\) be its smallest nearest center and set
\[
 m_{v,K}(o;C)=\{\widehat b_v(x)-q_C(\widehat b_v(x))\}^2
 +2\{\widehat b_v(x)-q_C(\widehat b_v(x))\}\widehat\zeta_v(o).
\]
Fit the codebook by the plain criterion
\[
 \widehat C_{v,K}
 =\operatorname*{lex\,min}\arg\min_{C\in\mathcal C_K}
 \frac1{|\mathcal Q_v|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal Q_v}
 \min_{c\in C}\{\widehat b_v(X_{n,i})-c\}^2.                                  \tag{E.1}
\]
The objective in (E.1) is continuous in \(C\), because it is a finite sum of minima of finitely many continuous functions, and \(\mathcal C_K\) is compact.  Thus its argmin is nonempty and compact.  Recursively minimizing the first, then second, and subsequent coordinates over the preceding compact argmin sets defines the displayed lexicographic selector; the same finite minimum construction applied to rational open sublevel sets makes it a Borel function of the fitting sample.  Hence (E.1) is a total deterministic measurable map.  Orthogonal correction is used only for evaluation.  Define the out-of-fold risk coefficients
\[
 \check W_{v,K}=\frac1{|\mathcal Q_v|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal Q_v}
 m_{v,K}(O_{n,i};\widehat C_{v,K}),
\]
and, for \(i\in\mathcal I_v\), set
\[
 \widehat m_{i,K}=m_{v,K}(O_{n,i};\widehat C_{v,K}),
 \qquad
 \widehat W_K=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat m_{i,K}.
\]
On \(\{\widehat W_1\neq0\}\), define
\[
 \widehat G_K=\frac{\widehat W_K-\widehat W_{K+1}}{\widehat W_1};
\]
on \(\{\widehat W_1=0\}\), set \(\widehat G_K=0\).  If \(i\in\mathcal I_v\) and \(\check W_{v,1}\neq0\), define
\[

 \frac{\widehat m_{i,K}-\widehat m_{i,K+1}}{\check W_{v,1}}
 -\frac{(\check W_{v,K}-\check W_{v,K+1})\widehat m_{i,1}}{\check W_{v,1}^2};
\]
if \(\check W_{v,1}=0\), set \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}=0\).  Finally set
\[

\]

\[

 \qquad

 \frac{\widehat\mu_{1,v}(x)-\widehat\mu_{0,v}(x)+1}{2}\right\}\right],
\]
and define, for \(o=(x,a,y)\),
\[
 \widehat\zeta_v(o)=\frac12\left[
 \frac{a\{y-\widehat\mu_{1,v}(x)\}}{\widehat e_v^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)}
 -\frac{(1-a)\{y-\widehat\mu_{0,v}(x)\}}{1-\widehat e_v^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)}\right].
\]
For \(C\in\mathcal C_K\), let \(q_C(u)\) be its smallest nearest center and set
\[
 m_{v,K}(o;C)=\{\widehat b_v(x)-q_C(\widehat b_v(x))\}^2
 +2\{\widehat b_v(x)-q_C(\widehat b_v(x))\}\widehat\zeta_v(o).
\]

\[
 \widehat C_{v,K}
 =\operatorname*{lex\,min}\arg\min_{C\in\mathcal C_K}
 \frac1{|\mathcal Q_v|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal Q_v}
 \min_{c\in C}\{\widehat b_v(X_{n,i})-c\}^2.                                  \tag{E.1}

proposed.statement:
Let \(m\geq2\), let \(Q_0,Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\) be probability measures on one measurable space with \(Q_j\ll Q_0\) for \(1\leq j\leq m\), and let \(\widehat J\) be any measurable map into \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).  Then
\[
 \frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m Q_j(\widehat J\neq j)
 \geq 1-\frac{m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)+\log2}{\log m}.
\]
The same inequality holds for randomized decoders after adjoining a randomization variable having one common law and independent of the observation under every \(Q_j\).

source.verbatim_statement: Lemma 2.10 (Fano’s lemma). Let P_0,P_1,...,P_M be probability measures on (X,A), M>=1. Then p_e,M <= M/(M+1) and g(p_e,M) >= log(M+1) - (M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=0}^M K(P_j,P), where P=(M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=0}^M P_j and g(x)=x log M+H(x). Equation (2.70): g(p_e,M) >= log(M+1) - (M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=1}^M K(P_j,P_0). Corollary 2.6: if (M+1)^{-1} sum_{j=1}^M K(P_j,P_0) <= alpha log M, then p_e,M >= [log(M+1)-log 2]/log M - alpha.
